subject: Intermittent app timeouts — return-path + MSS/conntrack triage
messages:
From: Network Ops <network_ops@netrix.com>
To: tessa.morgan@redwood.ai
Cc: rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-04-20T08:12:33-07:00
Subject: Users seeing intermittent timeouts to private deployment (Netrix prod)

Hi Tessa,

We started seeing intermittent timeouts from our app servers to the Redwood Private front door this morning (approx 07:50 PDT). Symptoms: TLS handshakes failing ~1-2% of requests, and a subset of long uploads (multipart file chunks) reset mid-transfer. Traceroute shows the path from our VPN concentrator -> customer edge -> transit -> Redwood VPC; we attached a traceroute and a small tcpdump capture from our side.

Immediate ask: can your NAT/gw team check for conntrack resource exhaustion or asymmetric return paths? We also saw MTU and ICMP fragments on the customer edge logs. Happy to hop on a call.

Thanks,
Sabrina Holt
Network Reliability Lead, Netrix Solutions

Attachments: traceroute_netrix_to_private_vpc.txt, tcpdump_sample_mss_drop.pcap
From: tessa.morgan@redwood.ai
To: Network Ops <network_ops@netrix.com>
Cc: rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, ethan_park@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-04-20T09:02:11-07:00
Subject: Re: Users seeing intermittent timeouts to private deployment (Netrix prod)

Hi Sabrina — thanks for the quick heads up and the captures.

We're triaging now. First pass: I asked infra to pull conntrack metrics and NAT gateway CPU/memory. Can you confirm whether Netrix is doing symmetric routing for return traffic (same eBGP pair/next-hop) or if you have any ECMP load balancing at the customer edge? Also please confirm whether you see ICMP unreachable (fragmentation-needed) to/from the Redwood VPC.

I'll update in ~30m with findings. If you'd like a bridge, ping me and I can spin one up.

- Tessa
Director, Customer Escalations | Redwood Inference
From: rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
To: tessa.morgan@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, ethan_park@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-04-20T09:27:54-07:00
Subject: Re: Users seeing intermittent timeouts to private deployment (Netrix prod)

Putting quick notes from infra/debug:
- NAT gateway (nat-gw-prod-3) shows conntrack table at 92% (peak) around 07:45-08:10 PT, with short spikes in SYN_RECV count suggesting many short-lived half-open sessions. We have a rule that drops entries older than 300s; GC is fine but churn is high.
- CPU on the gw spiked to 68% for a few minutes; no OOMs.
- IPs in question are behind Netrix's VPN (10.20.0.0/16 heading into our VPC). We see asymmetric routing for ~4% of flows: return path goes out via a different transit (transit-b) where the source NAT was not applied due to an ingress policy mismatch. That explains some of the TLS mismatches.
- I grabbed the tcpdump on the gw and see MSS/DF handling: victim flows show MSS clamped on the customer side but DF set, so fragmentation-needed ICMP not being delivered back consistently.

Immediate proposed mitigations:
1) Apply a temporary policy to enforce SNAT on both transit-a and transit-b gateways so return path is consistent (sticky SNAT).
2) Increase conntrack_max to 2x for the NAT cluster and tune tcp_time_wait to reduce churn.
3) Ask Netrix to clamp MSS to 1400 on their VPN concentrator for testing (reduces fragmentation).

I'll stage a canary change to apply SNAT on transit-b for 10:30 PT and monitor. ETA 30m.

- Rishi
Senior Network Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attached: fw-rule-diff-before-after.txt (planned rule add), tcpdump_sample_mss_drop.pcap (excerpt)
From: Network Ops <network_ops@netrix.com>
To: tessa.morgan@redwood.ai
Cc: rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-04-20T10:05:48-07:00
Subject: Re: Users seeing intermittent timeouts to private deployment (Netrix prod)

Thanks Rishi/Tessa — Confirmed: we do have ECMP at the customer edge but had not anticipated return path divergence within the carrier network. We enabled MSS clamp 1400 on the VPN concentrator at 09:50 PT and saw an immediate drop in fragmentation ICMPs.

We also saw the Netrix-side VPN concentrator log a burst of new connections from ephemeral ports around 07:40-08:05; we'll keep an eye and lower the idle timeout as a precaution.

Let us know when the SNAT policy is live and we'll run a set of synthetic uploads. We can also open a ticket with our carrier for the asymmetric return path but would prefer to validate with your config changes first.

Sabrina
From: tessa.morgan@redwood.ai
To: Network Ops <network_ops@netrix.com>
Cc: rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, ethan_park@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-04-21T16:47:02-07:00
Subject: Re: Users seeing intermittent timeouts to private deployment (Netrix prod)

Update/closure notes:

Action taken (Redwood):
- 2027-04-20 10:30 PT: Enabled consistent SNAT/sticky SNAT on transit-b for Netrix prefixes (10.20.0.0/16).
- 2027-04-20 10:35 PT: Increased conntrack_max on NAT cluster from 4M -> 8M and decreased conntrack TCP timeout for FIN_WAIT/TIME_WAIT where safe.
- Added explicit rule to allow ICMP type 3 code 4 (fragmentation needed) between Netrix AS and our VPC for PMTU signals.
- Monitored for 48h: TLS handshake failures dropped from ~1.8% -> 0.05%; long-upload resets dropped to near zero.

Action taken (Netrix):
- Enabled MSS clamp 1400 on VPN at 09:50 PT and reduced idle timeout on tunnel.

Follow-ups / Recommendations:
- Keep conntrack_max increase as permanent for this NAT cluster for the next quarter while traffic patterns stabilize.
- Engineering to add telemetry alerts for asymmetric routing detected by observing mismatched SNAT egresses per prefix (JIRA-RT-7682).
- Ops playbook: when customers report fragmentation + timeouts, ask for a traceroute and tcpdump and try MSS clamp as a short test.

Closing the escalation. Thanks to Netrix for fast collaboration and to Rishi/Ethan/Marissa for the quick remediation.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Director, Customer Escalations | Redwood Inference
